comment: Static IL patches applied to the player's sts2.dll by Spire.Patcher (tools/build_logic.py). Each replaces a Harmony patch from sts2-cli; handlers for 'redirect' ids are in logic/Spire.Logic/Hooks.cs. A missing non-optional target fails the build: that is the signal the game API moved (see docs/LOGIC_BUILD.md).

patches.note: Cuts the game logic off from its Godot UI layer: every call from logic into a UI class (namespace MegaCrit.Sts2.Core.Nodes.*, or any game class deriving from a Godot class, e.g. NDebugAudioManager) becomes a recorded presentation cue (sound, VFX, speech, music) with a safe default result.

The Godot UI layer never runs headless (the 'ui' patch redirects every call into it). Method bodies of the Godot-derived classes there (nodes, and what is nested in them) become a throw so the AOT builds do not compile the UI (console code size). Constructors stay, and plain helper classes in those namespaces (EpochComparer) are untouched. A 'headless: ...' NotSupportedException in a log means the logic reached UI code.

Game logic calls into Godot engine objects (scenes from the asset cache, tweens, nodes) that are null without the engine. A null receiver now skips the call with a safe default; non-null receivers (stub objects) behave as before.
Game code awaits Task.Delay for pacing (e.g. Amalgamator). A real timer would leave the adapter reporting a decision mid-effect; every call completes at once and records a 'wait' cue instead.
